events.label: Markets reopen post-Juneteenth; Hormuz Day-5 implementation check; Fed post-blackout speakers begin
events.note: First US equity session since June 18. DXY at the Monday open is the single most important data point — DXY rose to 100.75 on Juneteenth FX session (wrong direction for BUY gate). DXY below 99.00 on close would activate all three BUY conditions (VIX ✅, SPX ✅, DXY ❌→✅). If DXY holds above 100, HOLD low-conviction regime continues. If DXY spikes above 101.5 with SPX below 7,460, HOLD reverts to STEP_ASIDE. Fed post-FOMC blackout lifts this weekend — watch for hawkish Warsh remarks. BTC stop clock expected to confirm at UTC midnight June 19 — any crypto-to-equity correlation selling is an early Monday risk.

events.label: NVDA Annual Meeting (9 AM PT virtual) + Micron Q3 FY2026 earnings (after close) + S&P Global flash PMIs (9:45 AM ET)
events.note: Triple-catalyst day for the AI-semis complex. (1) NVDA Annual Meeting (9 AM PT): Jensen Huang to address AI demand trajectory, Taiwan $150B spending commitment, and post-$25B-debt-offering capex plan. Q2 guidance $91B is the anchor; HBM demand and Blackwell Ultra cadence are the key signals. (2) Micron Q3 FY2026 (after close): guided record revenue $33.5B ±$0.75B, gross margin ~81%, non-GAAP EPS $19.15 ±$0.40; AI/HBM memory absorbing all production capacity; SK Hynix HBM4E sample confirmation supports beat-and-raise thesis. NVDA Meeting + MU earnings on the same day = maximum AI-semis volatility of the week. (3) S&P Global flash PMIs: Services PMI > 53 = hawkish July FOMC hike pressure; PMI < 50 = paradoxically dovish.

events.label: May 2026 PCE inflation (BEA, 8:30 AM ET) + Weekly jobless claims (8:30 AM ET)
events.note: THE week's dominant risk event. Wells Fargo estimates: PCE +0.5% MoM, 4.1% YoY; core PCE +0.3% MoM, 3.4% YoY. A print at or above these estimates validates all 9 FOMC hike dots and could push the 30Y above the 5.00% regime trigger — forcing a HOLD→STEP_ASIDE downgrade. A dramatically soft print (core below 3.0%) = BUY upgrade pathway opens. Have exits and hedges sized before 8:30 AM ET. Simultaneously: weekly jobless claims — low claims = strong labor = hawkish hike odds spike.

events.label: Russell Reconstitution effective at close — ~$11T passive rebalancing
events.note: Russell 2000 annual reconstitution effective after June 26 close (trading begins June 29). ~$11 trillion in passive assets rebalancing simultaneously. 2026 is the first year of semi-annual reconstitution (June + December). Build positions in newly added names before June 24; take profits before Friday close if PCE on June 25 was hawkish. A hawkish PCE on June 25 + $11T passive rebalancing on June 26 = the most disorderly potential tape of Q3.

events.label: Q1 2026 GDP final revision (BEA, 8:30 AM ET)
events.note: Final revision to Q1 2026 GDP. Contextual data — rarely moves markets materially, but in the current CPI 4.2% / 9-hike-dot backdrop, an upward GDP revision reinforces the 'Fed can hike without recession' thesis. A downward miss would be paradoxically dovish.

events.label: June CPI release (est.) — most important inflation data of the summer
events.note: May CPI 4.2% triggered 9 FOMC hike dots and regime breach on June 17. June CPI (released ~July 14) is the next recalibration: if CPI holds ≥ 4.0%, hike probability for July 28-29 FOMC spikes materially; if CPI falls to ≤ 3.7% (aided by Iran-deal oil disinflation), the rate path softens and BUY regime can re-open with high conviction.

events.label: Next FOMC meeting (July 28-29) — rate hike now on the table; 9 of 18 hike dots from June
events.note: Nine of 18 FOMC officials projected at least one 2026 rate hike at the June 17 meeting. A 25-bps hike (3.50-3.75% → 3.75-4.00%) at this meeting is now priced at non-trivial probability. July CPI data (~July 14) is the primary input. Rate hike = BEARISH regime confirmation. Hold = regime-dependent on interim data.

events.label: Iran-US Islamabad Declaration 60-day deadline — Hormuz full reopening + sanctions relief
events.note: Deal operational from June 18 MOU signing; 60-day window expires August 13. Hormuz central route still has ~80 mines as of June 19 — mine-clearance measured in weeks. Nuclear talks postponed (confirmed June 19). Failure to meet the August 13 deadline = oil spike reversal and energy re-rally; key summer positioning watch.

events.label: SPCX first earnings as a public company (approx.) — Starlink ARR + Starship cadence
events.note: First print since the June 12 IPO. SPCX stop triggered June 18 at $174.90 (daily close below $185 stop); re-entry only on two consecutive closes above $185 on above-average volume. Watch Starlink subscriber/ARR growth and Starship launch cadence. Binary in both directions; date approximate pending company confirmation.

events.label: SPCX 180-day IPO lock-up expiry (approx.) — insider/early-investor float unlock
events.note: ~180 days after the June 12 debut, early investors and insiders can sell, materially expanding the ~4% public float. Lock-up expiries are a known supply overhang for hot IPOs; size accordingly into the window. Exact date pending the prospectus's stated terms.
